messages:
Kofi: odd late lunch thought 30 what would you pick as a guilty-pleasure soundtrack for reading a grim dystopian novel?
Maya: haha nice. I'd go upbeat pop to keep morale up. ABBA feels bizarrely comforting.
Ellen: counterpoint: synthpop with bright chords. Chloe x Halle or early M83 could work.
Raj: for me it's ska? upbeat horns while the world burns. ironic energy.
Kofi: options then: 1) upbeat disco/pop 2) bright synthpop 3) ironic ska 4) totally mismatched country ballads. react :one: :two: :three: :four: and drop short recs if you want
Maya: :one: ABBA   "Dancing Queen" on loop.
Ellen: :two: "Midnight City" vibes then maybe some Ladytron.
Raj: :three: early Specials. makes grim reading oddly buoyant.
Kofi: :four: route for maximal wrongness 3 Johnny Cash solitude between chapters.
PollBot: Poll created by Kofi: "Guilty soundtrack for dystopia"  1) Disco/Pop; 2) Bright synthpop; 3) Ska; 4) Country ballads. Ends in 2h.
Maya: voted :one:.
Ellen: voted :two:.
Raj: voted :three:.
Kofi: voted :four:.
Maya: also recs for book pairing: 'The Road' with country ballads is darkly poetic if you can handle the mood swing.
Ellen: 'Never Let Me Go' with synthpop gives it a weird, dreamlike tinge.
Raj: 'Parable of the Sower' reads great to ska somehow, gives you stubborn forward motion.
Kofi: thanks folks  I'll report back which mismatch made the bleak parts tolerable.
